notes: Each carrier and its payload file were produced by the vendor tool, not by CipherFlow's self-test writer. The OpenStego fixture uses the vendor's default compression and AES-128 encryption. A released OpenStego 0.7.2 or 0.8.6 distribution registers RandomLSB and DWTDugad, but not the sequential LSB plugin, so browser coverage uses RandomLSB; the Node self-test still covers the sequential layout. The JPHide fixtures come from JPHide 0.3 on Linux and JPHide/JPSeek 0.51 on Windows; the 0.51 pair covers a raw mode-1 carrier and a mode-3 carrier whose payload the tool stored as LZO1X.
